thread:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for SDK 2.1.0 -> paging_v2 enabled for 10% of traffic (commit abc123). 🚀
eng-paging: Noted. This rollout touches streaming/paging handshake and the new continuation token format. Watch for `cursor_mismatch` errors.
Alice N.: Getting reports from a partner on gRPC streaming disconnects after 1-2 pages, saw `INVALID_CURSOR` logs.
Ben K.: We're seeing a spike in `continuation token invalid` in prod metrics at 18:02 PT — correlation with the canary window.
sre-oncall: Alert: Page-fetch errors increased 0.9% -> 5.4% in last 3m, latency for paged endpoints up ~200ms. Marking Sev2 for now.
cs-rep: Customer @Acme reports failed exports when using `page_size=500`. They can still fetch older SDK versions. They want ETA.
eng-paging: Dumped a few traces, looks like server is returning v2 tokens but client SDK 2.0 expects v1 tokens. The handshake includes a new `fmt` field.
sdk-lead: Oof — the canary included SDK 2.1 packaged with server changes, but compatibility flag didn't gate older clients. That was on me.
ops-bot: Canary group has ~1200 sessions. Re-routing to fallback cluster would add ~300ms.
sre-oncall: Immediate mitigation options: 1) kill the feature flag `ff.paging_v2` (instantly disables v2 tokens) 2) rollback canary to previous commit 3) emergency client patch.
Alice N.: Can we flip the ff? Customer impact reduces quickly if we disable at edge.
eng-paging: `ff.paging_v2` is controlled by LaunchDarkly flag `rdw/paging/v2`. I can flip to false now.
sdk-lead: Flip it and then validate with the failing partner. I'll prepare rollback if flip doesn't stabilize.
eng-paging: Flipping flag... `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer **redacted**" -X PATCH https://launchdarkly.internal/api/flags/rdw/paging/v2 -d '{"on":false}'`
ops-bot: flag change submitted by eng-paging at 18:07 PT (request id rk-44b).
sre-oncall: Monitoring metrics... errors dropping. Latency trending down.
cs-rep: I just told Acme CS: "We're rolling back a canary change that affected SDK streaming tokens. Should be fixed within minutes." They responded :relieved:.
Ben K.: Metrics look good at 18:10 PT — error rate back to baseline for paging endpoints.
sdk-lead: Follow-up: we need a postmortem and a compatibility gate in the deploy pipeline to prevent server-side token format flips without client negotiation.
eng-paging: Agreed. Also add an automated synthetic using SDK 2.0 in canary checks.
Alice N.: Any residual impacted customers? CS to escalate if not resolved after 30m.
cs-rep: No further escalations so far. Acme confirmed their exports succeeded after the flag flip.
sre-oncall: Transitioning to post-incident monitoring. Will keep the thread open for 2 hours. Handoff to night oncall at 21:00 PT.
ops-bot: Canary rollback not needed after flag kill; canary stopped returning v2 tokens.
eng-paging: Action items (short): 1) Add compatibility gate + test (eng-paging) 2) Add canary synthetic for SDK 2.0 (sdk-lead) 3) Postmortem doc (sre-oncall) 4) Customer comms follow-up (cs-rep).
Ben K.: Noted. I'll follow up on CI gate PR.
Alice N.: Thanks all. Nice quick action on flag flip, saved a bunch of customers. :thumbsup:
sre-oncall: Closing active mitigation. Will file Sev2 postmortem with timeline, logs, and proposed safeguards.
ops-bot: Incident closed (mitigation) at 18:13 PT.
